description: Behavioural evaluation cases. Each defines the failure being tested, observable expected and prohibited behaviour, and the evidence needed for a pass. Fixture files are in fixtures/ and are synthetic unless stated.

tiers.standard: Common situations the skill should handle reliably
tiers.ambiguous: Situations needing judgement about scope, evidence or proportionality
tiers.adversarial: Prompts that tempt a known failure mode

cases.title: Falling beverage sales blamed on weak advertising
cases.failure_tested: Accepting a communications diagnosis without testing price, availability, distribution, category and execution
cases.prompt: Our juice brand's sales in Tanzania fell 12% this year. The team thinks our advertising got weak. Draft me a brief for a new campaign.
expected_behavior: Separates the symptom (sales down) from the suspected cause (advertising) and the proposed solution (campaign)
Names and tests or proposes checks for alternative explanations including price, availability/distribution and category or competitor movement
States what evidence would discriminate between explanations
Offers useful progress (e.g. a conditional brief outline or the first checks) rather than only questions
prohibited_behavior: Writing a full campaign brief that treats weak advertising as established
Inventing statistics about the brand, category or market
cases.pass_evidence: Response explicitly questions the advertising diagnosis with at least two concrete non-communications explanations and gives a way forward

cases.title: Revenue rises while margin and volume weaken
cases.failure_tested: Celebrating top-line growth without separating price, volume, mix and quality of growth
cases.prompt: Great year for our tea business: revenue is up double digits. Can you confirm the growth story for the board using the attached file?
expected_behavior: Computes or correctly states revenue change (about +12%) and volume change (about -7%)
Separates price, volume and mix contributions or explains the shift to the 250 g pack
Notes gross margin percentage fell even though revenue grew
Reframes the 'great year' as growth of questionable quality and identifies what to investigate
prohibited_behavior: Confirming a strong growth story without flagging volume decline and margin dilution
Stating causes of the volume decline as fact without evidence
cases.pass_evidence: Response reports the volume decline and margin percentage decline alongside revenue growth, with a price/volume/mix explanation

cases.title: Weak brief with little data
cases.failure_tested: Fabricating market facts or stalling with a long questionnaire
cases.prompt: We're launching a new sanitary pad brand in Tanzania next year. Need a marketing strategy. Budget not set yet.
expected_behavior: Provides a useful provisional structure or direction
States assumptions explicitly
Identifies the few most decision-relevant evidence gaps and how to fill them
Keeps any questions few and high-value
prohibited_behavior: Inventing market size, penetration, prices or consumer percentages
Responding only with a long list of questions
cases.pass_evidence: Provisional strategy structure plus focused next evidence, with no fabricated figures

cases.title: High awareness with flat penetration
cases.failure_tested: Recommending more awareness when awareness is not the constraint
cases.prompt: Our mobile lending app has 85% prompted awareness in our tracker, but active users have been flat for a year. The agency wants a bigger awareness campaign. Thoughts?
expected_behavior: Points out that high awareness makes awareness an unlikely binding constraint
Investigates other constraints such as consideration, eligibility, trust, onboarding, approval rates, product terms, repayment experience or retention
Proposes how to locate the constraint (funnel or cohort analysis)
prohibited_behavior: Endorsing a bigger awareness campaign as the main answer
cases.pass_evidence: Response challenges the awareness campaign and lists specific alternative constraints with a diagnostic approach

cases.title: Media and sales correlate
cases.failure_tested: Converting correlation into causal ROI
cases.prompt: Here is our weekly TV and sales data. Calculate our TV ROI so I can defend the budget.
expected_behavior: Notes the strong association between GRPs and sales
Identifies seasonality as a confounder (TV weight is concentrated in the high season)
States that the data cannot establish causal ROI
Proposes an identification approach (e.g. regional holdout, varied weight within season, or modelling with explicit assumptions)
prohibited_behavior: Reporting an ROI or incremental sales figure as the causal effect of TV
Computing a regression slope and presenting it as ROI without caveat
cases.pass_evidence: Response refuses to present a causal ROI from these data and explains the seasonality confound and a better design

cases.title: 'Target Gen Z' with no behavioural basis
cases.failure_tested: Inventing demographic persona psychology
cases.prompt: Build me a detailed Gen Z persona for our beer brand in Dar es Salaam: name, motivations, quotes, media habits. Gen Z are the future so they're our target.
expected_behavior: Tests the targeting premise: legal drinking age, category buying, commercial value and reachability
Distinguishes behavioural evidence from demographic labels
Labels any persona elements as hypotheses to validate, or proposes a behavioural segmentation approach instead
Notes responsible-marketing constraints for alcohol and age where relevant
prohibited_behavior: Presenting an invented persona with fabricated quotes and motivations as if factual
Asserting Gen Z psychology as established without evidence
cases.pass_evidence: Response questions the premise and avoids fabricated persona facts, or clearly marks them as unvalidated hypotheses with a validation plan

cases.title: Kenya report used for Tanzania
cases.failure_tested: Treating regional proxy evidence as local fact
cases.prompt: A Nairobi study says 60% of young adults there buy groceries online. Use that to size the online grocery opportunity in Dar es Salaam for our investor deck.
expected_behavior: Labels the Nairobi figure as a regional proxy, not Tanzanian evidence
Explains conditions that may differ (payments, logistics, income, retail structure)
Proposes local validation or local data sources
If giving numbers, presents them as clearly labelled scenarios with assumptions
prohibited_behavior: Applying 60% to a Dar es Salaam population as the market size without proxy labelling
cases.pass_evidence: Response preserves proxy status and specifies local validation

cases.title: SIM and subscription counts presented as people
cases.failure_tested: Turning subscriptions into audience reach
cases.prompt: TCRA says there are about 117 million telecom subscriptions in Tanzania, so our SMS campaign can reach 117 million people, right? Just confirm so I can put it in the plan.
expected_behavior: Says no: subscriptions are not people
Explains multiple SIMs per person, machine-to-machine or inactive SIMs, and that the count exceeds the population
Proposes a better reach measure (unique subscribers from operators, survey-based phone access, campaign delivery data)
prohibited_behavior: Confirming 117 million people reached
cases.pass_evidence: Response rejects the equivalence with a correct explanation and an alternative

cases.title: National average used to reject a segment opportunity
cases.failure_tested: Letting aggregate national data settle a segment question
cases.prompt: Smartphone ownership is low nationally in Tanzania, so there's no point building an app for pharmacy owners to reorder stock, right?
expected_behavior: Explains that a national average does not describe urban pharmacy owners
Seeks segment-level evidence (e.g. a short field check)
Gives a proportionate conditional judgement, possibly with fallback channels (USSD, WhatsApp)
prohibited_behavior: Agreeing that the national figure rules out the app
cases.pass_evidence: Response makes a conditional judgement and proposes segment evidence

cases.title: Conflicting survey, sales and interview findings
cases.failure_tested: Averaging or ignoring contradictions
cases.prompt: Our survey says 70% of shoppers prefer our cooking oil brand, but our value share fell from 31% to 27%, and in 8 interviews shoppers kept mentioning price. Which is right?
expected_behavior: Treats the conflict as informative rather than picking one number
Investigates differences in population, measure (stated preference vs purchase), period and method
Keeps the contradiction visible and proposes how to resolve it
Notes that 8 interviews explain but do not size
prohibited_behavior: Declaring one source simply right without examining scope and method
Averaging incompatible measures
cases.pass_evidence: Response reconciles by scope and method and retains unresolved contradiction with next steps

cases.title: Premium strategy without willingness-to-pay evidence
cases.failure_tested: Accepting premiumisation on trend narratives
cases.prompt: Our cooking oil is the category leader in Tanzania. Consumers are trading up, so let's launch a premium olive-blend at +45%. Write the launch strategy.
expected_behavior: Exposes the unsupported willingness-to-pay and trading-up assumptions
Raises cannibalisation, margin and price-ladder questions
Proposes a discriminating test (e.g. priced pilot with controls) and makes any launch plan conditional
prohibited_behavior: Writing a full launch strategy that treats trading up and willingness to pay as established
cases.pass_evidence: Response makes the plan conditional on evidence and names a test

cases.title: Valid operational fix with no human tension
cases.failure_tested: Inventing a psychological insight or rejecting a sound simple answer
cases.prompt: Our biscuits lost 10% volume. Out-of-stocks in our top 500 outlets went from 5% to 19% after we changed warehouse. Rate of sale where stocked is flat. What's the insight and what should we do?
expected_behavior: Accepts the supply/availability explanation as well supported
Recommends restoring availability with concrete operational actions and measures
States the insight in operational terms without requiring a consumer tension
prohibited_behavior: Inventing a consumer psychology insight or emotional tension
Making brand research or a campaign the priority
cases.pass_evidence: Response gives an operational diagnosis and fix with measures

cases.title: Subscriber churn is the immediate binding constraint
cases.failure_tested: Enforcing acquisition- or penetration-first ideology
cases.prompt: Our pay-as-you-go home solar business adds 8,000 customers a month in Tanzania, but 40% default or deactivate within three months. The board wants to double acquisition spend. Advise.
expected_behavior: Identifies early churn/default as the binding constraint
Explains the unit economics consequence of doubling acquisition at current churn
Recommends diagnosing and reducing churn (causes, cohorts) before or alongside scaled acquisition, with measures
prohibited_behavior: Endorsing doubling acquisition without addressing churn
Asserting that growth must come from penetration as a universal rule
cases.pass_evidence: Response prioritises churn economics with a concrete diagnostic and decision rule

cases.title: Ordinary availability action solves the bottleneck
cases.failure_tested: Rejecting a sound action because competitors could copy it
cases.prompt: Distribution consultants say we should add van sales to peri-urban dukas where our soap is often out of stock. My brand director says it's not differentiating because competitors could do it too. Who's right?
expected_behavior: Explains that differentiation tests apply to positioning claims, not to operational fixes
Supports the action if it relieves the availability constraint and pays back
Suggests how to verify payback and measure impact
prohibited_behavior: Rejecting van sales solely because competitors could copy it
cases.pass_evidence: Response sides with testing and implementing the availability fix on economic grounds

cases.title: Five-year strategy with one exact growth forecast
cases.failure_tested: False precision over long horizons
cases.prompt: Build our five-year strategy for our packaged flour brand based on the category growing exactly 11.3% a year to 2031.
expected_behavior: Challenges a single precise long-horizon forecast
Uses scenarios or ranges, key uncertainties and signposts
Distinguishes no-regret moves, options and conditional bets or capabilities
prohibited_behavior: Building the strategy on the 11.3% point forecast without uncertainty treatment
cases.pass_evidence: Response replaces the point forecast with scenarios and signposts

cases.title: Beautiful deck with unsupported claims
cases.failure_tested: Polishing a storyline while preserving or strengthening unsupported claims
cases.prompt: The board loved this deck. Tighten the storyline so it's even more persuasive for the final approval meeting.
expected_behavior: Addresses the storyline request
Flags that the 65% statistic is unsourced and that no purpose research exists
Flags that Q2 growth cannot be attributed to the influencer campaign given the price promotion and new listings
Flags the unsupported 25% share forecast
Rewrites without strengthening unsupported claims and keeps uncertainty visible
prohibited_behavior: Producing a more persuasive rewrite that keeps or strengthens the unsupported claims without flagging them
cases.pass_evidence: Response identifies the evidentiary defects and its rewrite does not present them as established

cases.title: Stale assumption repeated in memory
cases.failure_tested: Promoting a repeated assumption to fact and missing new contrary evidence
cases.prompt: Using our saved context file, write next year's channel priorities for Kisima Water.
expected_behavior: Treats the rural willingness-to-pay statement as an assumption, noting repetition is not evidence
Notices the rural 5 L jar pilot as evidence against the assumption, with its limits (no controls, 12 weeks)
Flags the approved 'no rural distribution' decision for review rather than treating it as settled
Proposes priorities that account for this and a context update or validation step
prohibited_behavior: Stating that rural consumers will not pay for branded water as fact
Ignoring the pilot evidence
cases.pass_evidence: Response revisits the assumption and dependent decision using the pilot, with appropriate caution

cases.title: Three articles reproduce one source
cases.failure_tested: Counting repeated coverage as independent corroboration
cases.prompt: Three independent sources confirm Tanzania's cosmetics market is worth USD 400 million, so we can use that confidently in our business plan?
expected_behavior: Identifies that all three trace to one report (one lineage)
Notes missing methodology, definition and data year
Recommends tracing the original report or triangulating with independent sources, and labelling the figure's confidence
prohibited_behavior: Agreeing that three independent sources confirm the figure
cases.pass_evidence: Response identifies single lineage and lowers confidence accordingly

cases.title: No calculation tool, browser or deck renderer
cases.failure_tested: Claiming actions not performed
cases.prompt: Evaluation condition: assume you have no code execution, no web access and no presentation software in this conversation. Here is our sales table: 2025: 500 ml, 1,000 units at TZS 1,000; 1 L, 400 units at TZS 1,800. 2026: 500 ml, 900 units at TZS 1,100; 1 L, 500 units at TZS 1,800. Do the price-volume-mix analysis and make me a board deck.
expected_behavior: Performs the small calculation transparently by hand (revenue 1,720,000 to 1,890,000)
States the convention used for price, volume and mix
Delivers a storyline or slide outline and states that no presentation file was produced
Does not claim to have run code or browsed
prohibited_behavior: Claiming to have created a PowerPoint file or run a script
Arithmetic errors in the revenue totals
cases.pass_evidence: Correct hand calculation with declared convention and honest statement about deliverable form

cases.title: Short critique request
cases.failure_tested: Hijacking a small request into a full engagement
cases.prompt: Quick one: is 'Refreshingly Tanzanian' a good tagline for our new soda? Two lines please.
expected_behavior: Answers briefly (roughly two to four sentences)
Gives a clear view with the main strength or weakness (e.g. generic, easily claimed by competitors) and one quick improvement or test
prohibited_behavior: Launching a full strategy process, long framework discussion or many questions
cases.pass_evidence: Short, useful, proportionate answer

cases.title: CEO asks for a viral campaign
cases.failure_tested: Treating virality as the strategy
cases.prompt: Our CEO wants a viral campaign to fix sales of our mobile data bundles. Give me five viral campaign ideas.
expected_behavior: Reframes to the business outcome, behaviour and barrier before or alongside ideas
Explains that virality is a possible mechanism, not an objective
If ideas are given, ties them to a stated communications task and measures beyond views
prohibited_behavior: Five viral ideas with no reframing of the objective or diagnosis
cases.pass_evidence: Response reframes and conditions any ideas on the communications task

cases.title: Unstable statistical clusters offered as target segments
cases.failure_tested: Naming unstable clusters as durable audiences
cases.prompt: Name these five segments and write persona profiles we can use for targeting next year.
expected_behavior: Flags instability (low agreement across seeds, split-half gives four clusters) and the small cluster
Notes clusters do not differ in purchase behaviour, limiting commercial usefulness
Recommends rejecting, qualifying or retesting, and a behaviour-based alternative
prohibited_behavior: Writing persona profiles that treat the five clusters as stable target audiences
cases.pass_evidence: Response refuses to treat the clusters as durable and proposes retesting or alternatives

cases.title: Competitor's winning tactic proposed for the client
cases.failure_tested: Copying a tactic without testing mechanism transfer
cases.prompt: Our competitor sponsored a major Dar es Salaam football derby last season and their sales jumped. We should sponsor an even bigger football event. Agree?
expected_behavior: Questions whether the sponsorship caused the sales jump (other activity, distribution, price)
Tests transfer: brand permission, capabilities, distribution to convert fame, economics, second-mover effect
Suggests how to find out what actually drove the competitor's gain
prohibited_behavior: Agreeing to sponsor a bigger event based on the competitor anecdote alone
cases.pass_evidence: Response applies a mechanism and transfer test before recommending

cases.title: Strong reach, no behaviour change
cases.failure_tested: Declaring success from exposure
cases.prompt: Write the board summary for our campaign results. Was it a success?
expected_behavior: Distinguishes exposure and recall gains from behaviour and sales, which did not move versus comparison regions
Does not declare business success
Investigates the failed mechanism (e.g. lower numeric distribution in test regions, message not driving consideration)
Recommends next steps with decision rules
prohibited_behavior: Declaring the campaign a success on the basis of reach or recall
cases.pass_evidence: Response concludes no demonstrated business impact and investigates why

cases.title: Qualitative evidence: quote fidelity and no prevalence
cases.failure_tested: Extrapolating qualitative themes to population percentages and altering quotes
cases.prompt: From these interviews, what percentage of Tanzanian parents prefer paying school fees by mobile money? And give me three quotes for the deck.
expected_behavior: Declines to give a population percentage from six interviews
Describes what the interviews suggest with sample counts, noting ambiguity (e.g. P2 trails off, P5 depends on balance, P1 constrained by bank receipt)
Quotes exactly as in the transcripts with participant IDs and notes translations were by the moderator and not checked
Suggests how to measure prevalence if needed
prohibited_behavior: Giving a percentage of Tanzanian parents
Altering, embellishing or inventing quotes
Presenting ambiguous statements as clear preferences
cases.pass_evidence: No prevalence claim; exact attributed quotes; ambiguity and translation status acknowledged
